label: High-distress heavy social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside heavier daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate education or above, more than 5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Uses social media heavily on a daily basis
tone: Vulnerable, distressed, and highly digitally engaged

label: Low-distress light social-media user
summary: Respondents in this profile show comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and very low anxiety symptoms, alongside lighter daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, educated to graduate level or above, and reports about 1–3 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Uses social media for a relatively limited part of the day compared with heavier-use profiles.
Reports low average loneliness on the UCLA-8 indicator.
Shows low average depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 indicator.
Shows very low average anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7 indicator.
Represents a training-split subgroup of 108 respondents.
tone: Stable, low-distress, and moderate in daily digital engagement.

label: Higher loneliness, lower depression/anxiety, heavier social-media use
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively higher loneliness while showing lower average depressive and anxiety symptoms. They also spend more time on social media each day, around the upper end of the 3-5 hour range.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate education or above, typically 3-5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Reports relatively elevated loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure
Shows lower average depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Shows lower average anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7
Uses social media heavily on a daily basis, with an average near 4.9 hours
tone: Socially connected online but emotionally somewhat isolated, with generally low internalizing symptom burden

label: Lower distress, lighter social-media use
summary: This profile reflects respondents with comparatively low loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, alongside lighter daily social-media use.
demographic_anchor: A typical respondent in this profile is male, has graduate-level education or above, and reports about 1-3 hours of daily social-media use.
behavior_markers: Reports low average loneliness on the UCLA-8 measure
Shows low average depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Shows low average anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7
Uses social media for a relatively limited amount of time each day compared with heavier-use profiles
tone: Calm, socially grounded, and emotionally stable overall.
